index.heroSubtitle: Train with purpose, build strength, and make every session count.
index.introText: IRON ZONE is a premium fitness and personal training facility built around three simple ideas: serious equipment, certified coaches, and a plan for every member. Whether you are setting foot on the gym floor for the first time or chasing a new personal record, the space and the coaching are designed so that every single session counts.
index.introText2: The floor covers the full spectrum of strength work: free-weight platforms for barbell lifts, machine circuits for hypertrophy, dedicated cardio and functional zones, and a studio that hosts group classes throughout the week. Equipment is chosen for reliability rather than novelty, so the tools you depend on are always calibrated, maintained, and ready to use.
index.introText3: Every membership starts with an onboarding session. A coach reviews your goals, your movement history, and the time you can realistically give each week, then builds a training split you can actually sustain. From that point the plan evolves with your progress - through personal training, small-group classes, or self-directed sessions with our coaches on hand for technique checks and programming questions.
index.introAlt: Members training on the IRON ZONE gym floor
index.benefitsIntro: Training benefits are not a list of miracles. What follows are the results of a well-equipped floor, a plan you can follow, and coaches who tell you the truth about your numbers - measured over months, not weekends.
index.benefit1Text: Progressive barbell and machine work that builds usable strength and adds lean muscle over months rather than weeks. Loads and rep ranges are set to match the level you are actually at today.
index.benefit1Alt: Athlete lifting weights during a strength session
index.benefit2Text: One coach, one written plan, and honest correction on the lifts that matter. The hour goes into technique and programme adjustments, not into empty encouragement.
index.benefit2Alt: Personal trainer coaching a member one-on-one
index.benefit3Text: Coach-led sessions in a small group. This is often the practical middle ground: the structure of a class, with just enough attention to correct your form as you go.
index.benefit3Alt: High-energy group fitness class in progress
index.benefit4Text: Steady zone-based cardio and circuit work that builds a base your body can actually hold on to - and that shortens the recovery time between the heavier sessions.
index.benefit4Alt: Member on a cardio machine during a conditioning session
index.benefit5Text: Warm-ups, mobility work, and assisted stretching. Unglamorous, but it is the habit that keeps people training for years instead of months.
index.benefit5Alt: Member stretching on a mat during a mobility class
index.benefit6Text: Carrying, pushing, pulling, and rotating with loads that match daily life - the part of fitness that shows up outside the gym, on stairs, with a heavy bag, or after a long day at a desk.
index.benefit6Alt: Member carrying a weight during a functional training circuit
index.benefitsNote: Results are easier to keep when you can see them, so every membership comes with a workout log that records your sessions locally in your browser - you and your coach can compare weeks instead of guessing.

membership.title: Membership Plans
membership.note: *Prices in Egyptian pounds (EGP) — sample/demo content until verified
membership.faqA1: Memberships run month to month and do not lock you into a long contract. The prices on this page are demonstration figures, so read them as an illustration of the offer rather than a live quote.
membership.faqA2: In a real gym you would cancel at any time with no exit fee and keep access until the end of the month you paid for. This site is a demonstration, so the policy is only described here to show what the page would say.
membership.faqQ3: Do I need experience to start training?
membership.faqA3: No. Most members start with the fundamentals, and your onboarding session covers the basics before you touch a barbell. If you have trained before, your plan simply begins at a higher level.
membership.faqQ4: How many sessions a week should I attend?
membership.faqA4: Two to four sessions a week is where most members settle. Consistency matters more than the number: keep roughly the same slots each week and progress the loads slowly, rather than training hard for a few days and then stopping.
membership.faqQ5: Is personal training included in every plan?
membership.faqA5: No. Personal training is part of the Elite plan. Starter includes full access to the gym floor and the group classes, Pro adds priority booking and nutrition guidance, and a coach can also be booked by the hour with any plan.
membership.faqQ6: What should I bring to my first session?
membership.faqA6: Training clothes, flat shoes with a grippy sole, a water bottle, and a towel. We provide the equipment, but arrive ten minutes early for the onboarding and a quick tour of the floor.
membership.faqQ7: What happens if I miss a few weeks?
membership.faqA7: Nothing breaks and nobody chases you. Come back, tell your coach where you stopped, and the plan continues from the sessions you logged. A broken streak is a normal part of training - the goal is to still be training a year from now.
membership.faqA8: The first few weeks usually bring better technique and more stamina on the machines. Visible changes in strength and body composition take two to three months of consistent work, and they depend on nutrition and sleep as much as on the sessions themselves.

alex.bio: Ahmed has spent nearly a decade helping people move better and grow stronger. He blends classic strength training with functional movement, and is known for patient, step-by-step coaching that suits complete beginners and experienced lifters alike.
achievements: Built Iron Zone's beginner strength program

sarah.bio: Mariam is a high-energy cardio coach who makes hard sessions feel achievable. Her HIIT classes combine intervals, bodyweight circuits and upbeat music, and she specialises in building endurance for people returning to fitness.

mike.bio: Mahmoud is a competitive powerlifter with over a decade on the platform. He coaches the squat, bench and deadlift with precise technique work and smart programming, and has guided dozens of lifters to their first competition.

nina.bio: Nour brings calm, focused energy to every session. A 500-hour certified yoga teacher, she helps athletes and desk workers improve mobility, breathing and recovery, with classes that adapt to every level.

tom.bio: Omar focuses on beginners and busy professionals who want simple, sustainable progress. He builds confidence with clear technique, realistic goals and accountability, so training becomes a habit rather than a chore.

emma.bio: Salma leads some of the most energetic classes at Iron Zone. With a background in boxing fitness and group training, she mixes cardio, core work and conditioning into sessions that are challenging but always fun.
